rules.rule: A daily move at least 3 times the stock's normal daily move (a robust standard deviation of the prior 49 days).
Daily volume at least 3 times the average of the prior 50 days.
Implied growth moves at least 2 points over 5 trading days.
Results, deals and leadership changes from 8-K filings (items 2.02, 1.01, 2.01 and 5.02), checked after each close, plus votes and other dates I log with a source.
At least 10 Google News articles about the company in a day and at least 3 times its usual count (the median of the prior 20 days, once there are 10 days of history).
Each signal fades by 15% a trading day, so a name stays in play for about a week unless something new happens.

season.entry_rule: Equal weight at the Oct 14, 2026 close (first close after this lock).
season.rebalance_rule: First trading day of each month: hold the 5 names with the most negative gap, equal weight; deal-price names excluded.

excluded.VRSK: SEC data feed returned empty for Verisk

notes: Each month I value every company with only the filings public by that month-end, at that month-end's price.

The backtest values equity directly: cash flow from operations minus capex, discounted at the cost of equity. It needs fewer inputs than the live model; on today's data the two rank the names almost identically (Spearman rank correlation 0.965).
The anchor is past revenue growth only (there is no free archive of old analyst forecasts), using years with growth between -20% and +25% so acquisitions don't count as growth.
Five names with the most negative gap are held for a month, equal weight, against an equal-weight portfolio of every name, with 0.10% charged on each unit of turnover.

COVID: Feb 2020 to Mar 2021 is reported separately. Variant two replaces fiscal 2020-21 revenue and margins with a straight line from 2019 to 2022. Variant three also floors the risk-free rate at 2.5% in that window, the normalized rate Kroll recommended from June 30, 2020.

The 90% ranges come from a circular block bootstrap: 4,000 reshuffles of 6-month blocks of the monthly results, wrapping at the end so every month is equally likely to be drawn. With only 14 COVID months, read that window's range as a direction, not a size.

writeups.title: Season 1 opener: the three biggest gaps
writeups.dek: Why the screen likes TMX, Cboe and Tradeweb, and what would make me wrong. Written at the lock, before the first close.

items.title: TMX Group: the gap is real, but part of it is purchased revenue
paras: At the lock, the price implied 1.4% a year of revenue growth for five years. My anchor is 15.0%, which is the analysts' three-year forecast on its own: TMX's past growth isn't comparable because VettaFi was consolidated in 2024 and TMX bought Cboe Australia this August.

That forecast includes revenue TMX bought, so the organic gap is narrower than the 13.6 points shown. The discount rate matters too. TMX's cost of capital is low at 6.4% because Canadian rates are low. At one point higher, implied growth rises to 5.3%.
What would prove me wrong: organic revenue growth below about 5% in the next two quarterly reports, or a pending deal falling apart.

items.title: Cboe: priced for shrinking net revenue
paras: At the lock, the price implied net revenue falling 1.8% a year for five years. My anchor is 10.4%: past net revenue growth of 14.7% and a forward estimate of 6.0%.

Two things make me cautious. Options volumes swing with volatility, so a few busy years can flatter past growth. And Cboe is selling Cboe Australia and Cboe Canada to TMX, which shrinks revenue. Trailing free cash flow is 68.2% of net revenue, above operating margin, so some of it may be timing. If that margin is too high, implied growth is understated.
What would prove me wrong: net revenue falling in the next two quarters once the sale closes.

items.title: Tradeweb: a growth platform priced like a utility
paras: At the lock, the price implied 2.9% a year of revenue growth. Tradeweb grew 17.3% a year from fiscal 2021, and analysts expect 12.1%. My anchor, the average, is 14.7%.

The market may be pricing slower bond and rates trading volumes and fee pressure, and past growth includes bolt-on purchases. But Tradeweb has net cash and a 51.8% free-cash-flow margin. Even at a cost of capital one point higher (8.8%), implied growth is only 6.2%.
What would prove me wrong: average daily volume falling year over year for two quarters in a row.
